source_verification.title: WNT1 mutations in early-onset osteoporosis and osteogenesis imperfecta
Mutations in WNT1 cause different forms of bone fragility

second_answer_attack.resolution: SERPINH1 loss produces a collagen-chaperone defect and can cause recessive OI, but the stem directly supplies biallelic WNT1 loss in severely affected children plus low bone mass in a heterozygous parent. That dosage pattern and genotype localize the defect to reduced WNT1-dependent canonical beta-catenin signaling.

blind_audit.rationale: Human WNT1 loss-of-function variants impair canonical Wnt pathway activation and osteoblast function. Biallelic loss produces a severe recessive OI phenotype, while heterozygous variants can produce early-onset osteoporosis, matching the dose-dependent family pattern in the vignette. Strongest alternative resolved: SERPINH1 loss produces a collagen-chaperone defect and can cause recessive OI, but the stem directly supplies biallelic WNT1 loss in severely affected children plus low bone mass in a heterozygous parent. That dosage pattern and genotype localize the defect to reduced WNT1-dependent canonical beta-catenin signaling.
